requirements.text: The game is called 'Crumb Chase'.
requirements.check: The game window title displays 'Crumb Chase'.
requirements.quote: Create a small one-screen maze game called "Crumb Chase".

requirements.text: The player controls a little green mouse.
requirements.check: A green mouse shape is visible on screen.
requirements.quote: The player is a little green mouse

requirements.text: The game features a 15x15 tile maze with walls.
requirements.check: A 15x15 grid of tiles is displayed, with some tiles rendered as walls.
requirements.quote: in a 15 by 15 tile maze with walls

requirements.text: The mouse starts in an open corridor.
requirements.check: At the start of the game, the mouse is positioned on an open tile with adjacent open tiles in at least two directions.
requirements.quote: the mouse starts in an open corridor where it can move in all four directions.

requirements.text: Arrow keys turn the mouse up, down, left, or right.
requirements.check: Pressing an arrow key changes the mouse's intended direction of movement.
requirements.quote: The arrow keys turn the mouse up, down, left or right

requirements.text: The mouse glides smoothly from tile to tile in its chosen direction until it hits a wall.
requirements.check: After pressing an arrow key, the mouse moves continuously in that direction, visually traversing tiles smoothly, until it reaches a wall tile.
requirements.quote: and it glides smoothly from tile to tile in that direction until it hits a wall.

requirements.text: The mouse's movement includes a squash-and-stretch animation.
requirements.check: When the mouse moves, its shape visibly deforms (squashes and stretches) during the transition between tiles.
requirements.quote: with a squash-and-stretch animation

requirements.text: Every open tile starts with a small cheese crumb.
requirements.check: All non-wall tiles initially display a small cheese crumb.
requirements.quote: Every open tile starts with a small cheese crumb

requirements.text: Eating a crumb adds 10 points.
requirements.check: When the mouse moves onto a tile with a crumb, the score increases by 10.
requirements.quote: eating a crumb adds 10 points

requirements.text: Eating a crumb causes a sparkle particle burst.
requirements.check: When a crumb is eaten, a visual particle effect appears briefly at the crumb's location.
requirements.quote: and pops it with a little sparkle particle burst.

requirements.text: Two cats chase the mouse through the maze.
requirements.check: Two distinct cat shapes are visible and move independently.
requirements.quote: Two cats chase the mouse through the maze

requirements.text: Cats slide smoothly between tiles.
requirements.check: Cats move continuously, visually traversing tiles smoothly.
requirements.quote: sliding smoothly between tiles

requirements.text: Cats choose the direction toward the mouse at each junction.
requirements.check: When a cat reaches a junction, it moves in the direction that reduces its distance to the mouse.
requirements.quote: and choosing the direction toward the mouse at each junction.

requirements.text: If a cat touches the mouse, the mouse loses a life.
requirements.check: When a cat's position overlaps with the mouse's position, the mouse's life count decreases by one.
requirements.quote: If a cat touches the mouse, the mouse loses a life

requirements.text: Losing a life triggers a short spin-and-fade animation for the mouse.
requirements.check: Upon losing a life, the mouse visibly spins and fades out before reappearing.
requirements.quote: with a short spin-and-fade animation

requirements.text: After losing a life, everyone returns to their start tiles.
requirements.check: After a collision, the mouse and both cats reset to their initial positions.
requirements.quote: and everyone returns to their start tiles.

requirements.text: The mouse has 3 lives.
requirements.check: The lives counter starts at 3.
requirements.quote: The mouse has 3 lives.

requirements.text: A level designer can redraw maze walls visually as a tile map.
requirements.check: The game includes a separate mode or tool that allows visual editing of the maze layout.
requirements.quote: A level designer should be able to redraw the maze walls visually as a tile map

requirements.text: A level designer can preview the level without touching code.
requirements.check: After editing the maze, the designer can immediately play or view the level without recompiling or modifying source code.
requirements.quote: and preview the level without touching code.

requirements.text: Eating every crumb wins the game.
requirements.check: When the last crumb is eaten, the game transitions to a 'WIN' state.
requirements.quote: Eating every crumb wins the game

requirements.text: Losing all lives ends the game.
requirements.check: When the mouse's lives reach 0, the game transitions to a 'GAME OVER' state.
requirements.quote: losing all lives ends the game.

requirements.text: The score and lives are shown at the top of the window.
requirements.check: Text displaying the current score and remaining lives is visible at the top of the game screen.
requirements.quote: Show the score and lives at the top of the window.

requirements.text: When the game is won or over, show WIN or GAME OVER with the final score.
requirements.check: Upon winning or losing, the screen displays 'WIN' or 'GAME OVER' along with the final score.
requirements.quote: When the game is won or over, show WIN or GAME OVER with the final score

requirements.text: When the game is won or over, freeze the game.
requirements.check: After winning or losing, all game movement and interaction (except restart/quit) ceases.
requirements.quote: and freeze the game.

requirements.text: Press R to restart with 3 lives and score 0.
requirements.check: Pressing 'R' resets the game to its initial state: mouse and cats at start, 3 lives, 0 score, all crumbs present.
requirements.quote: Press R to restart with 3 lives and score 0

requirements.text: Press Escape to quit.
requirements.check: Pressing 'Escape' closes the game window.
requirements.quote: and Escape to quit.

requirements.text: Print a line to the console every time a control takes effect: TURN UP, TURN DOWN, TURN LEFT, TURN RIGHT, RESTART and QUIT.
requirements.check: The console outputs 'TURN UP', 'TURN DOWN', 'TURN LEFT', 'TURN RIGHT', 'RESTART', or 'QUIT' when the corresponding action occurs.
requirements.quote: Print a line to the console every time a control takes effect: TURN UP, TURN DOWN, TURN LEFT, TURN RIGHT, RESTART and QUIT

requirements.text: Print WIN or GAME OVER to the console when the game ends.
requirements.check: The console outputs 'WIN' or 'GAME OVER' when the game reaches its respective end state.
requirements.quote: and print WIN or GAME OVER when the game ends.

requirements.text: Use plain coloured shapes only; no images or sounds.
requirements.check: All visual elements are rendered using basic geometric shapes and solid colors, with no loaded image files or audio playback.
requirements.quote: Use plain coloured shapes only; no images or sounds.

files.purpose: Empty file to mark game as a Python package.
Main Godot scene file, containing the game's root node and initial setup.
Main script for game logic, handling game state, input, and scene transitions.
Script for the player mouse, handling movement, animation, and collision with crumbs/cats.
Script for the enemy cats, handling movement, AI, and collision with the mouse.
Script for generating and managing the maze grid, walls, and crumbs.
Script for individual cheese crumbs, handling collection and particle effects.
Script for displaying score, lives, and game over/win messages.
Godot scene for the visual level editor.
Script for the level editor logic, handling tile map editing and saving/loading levels.

assets.strategy_rationale: The spec explicitly states 'Use plain coloured shapes only; no images or sounds.', so all assets will be drawn procedurally in code.

level_editor.summary: Visual level editor for maze walls.
level_editor.detail: A separate Godot scene and script will provide a visual interface for a level designer to draw maze walls on a tile map. It will allow saving and loading maze configurations, and a 'preview' function will launch the main game scene with the edited maze data. This will be implemented as a separate executable or a mode within the main game that can be accessed without code changes.

architecture.test_input_example: Press RIGHT, then UP, then LEFT, then DOWN, collecting crumbs. If a cat approaches, try to evade. If caught, observe life loss and reset. Continue until all crumbs are eaten (WIN) or all lives are lost (GAME OVER). Press R to restart, then ESCAPE to quit.
